findings.body: The reuse check proves only that a row and total have the same coordinate; it never compares their `actual.value` or `availableActualSubtotal.value`. A singleton filtered row can therefore share the total's `drilldownId` while displaying a different amount, even though the handle's `matchingActualTotal` can reconcile to only one of them. This violates the requirement that every clickable Actual open its matching transactions. Reject shared handles unless both scope and exact Actual value/state match, and add an unequal-value negative case; the existing positive fixture manually makes the values equal but does not enforce that invariant.
findings.title: Not done: shared drill handles must bind the same exact Actual
